Headline: Anthropic raises $65 billion, nears $1T valuation ahead of IPO | TechCrunch
Summary: Anthropic has raised $65 billion in a funding round, bringing its valuation close to $1 trillion ahead of a potential IPO. This significant investment underscores strong investor confidence in Anthropic's future.
Why it matters (BD): Anthropic's massive $65 billion funding round and near $1 trillion valuation signals a major competitive move, solidifying its position as a dominant AI lab and intensifying the race for market leadership, while also creating potential strategic partnership opportunities for companies looking to align with a top-tier AI provider.

For BD and partnerships professionals, this war chest signals a massive acceleration in enterprise-grade deployments and opens up high-stakes strategic integration opportunities across the tech stack.

content.what_changed: On May 28, 2026, Anthropic closed a $65 billion Series H funding round at a $965 billion post-money valuation, co-led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, Sequoia Capital, Capital Group, Coatue, and D1 Capital Partners. The round included strategic infrastructure investments from Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron, alongside $15 billion in hyperscaler commitments, and coincided with the launch of Claude Opus 4.8.
key_facts: Anthropic raised $65 billion in a Series H round on May 28, 2026, at a $965 billion post-money valuation.

The round was co-led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, Sequoia Capital, Capital Group, Coatue, and D1 Capital Partners, with additional participation from Baillie Gifford, Blackstone, Brookfield, D.E. Shaw Ventures, DST Global, and Fidelity.
Anthropic's run-rate revenue crossed $47 billion in May 2026, with the company projecting a 130% revenue surge to reach its first operating profit.
Strategic infrastructure partners Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron participated, alongside $15 billion in hyperscaler commitments including $5 billion from Amazon.
Anthropic's $965 billion valuation surpasses OpenAI's $852 billion post-money valuation from its March 2026 round.
content.bd_relevance: Anthropic stated it will use the new capital to 'scale the products and partnerships our customers rely on,' signaling aggressive enterprise partnership expansion — the narrow pre-IPO window is the optimal time to lock in strategic deals before public-market scrutiny shifts priorities. The inclusion of Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron as infrastructure partners creates new co-sell and integration opportunities for AI companies in the compute and hardware ecosystem.
content.headline: Anthropic Raises $65B at $965B Valuation, Leapfrogs OpenAI Ahead of IPO
content.why_it_matters: Anthropic's $965B valuation now exceeds OpenAI's $852B, flipping the longstanding hierarchy of AI startup valuations and confirming that the race to public markets will be a two-horse contest with massive capital advantages on both sides. The sheer scale of this round — and Anthropic's projected path to profitability — signals that the AI market is entering a phase where only entities with tens of billions in war chest can compete for enterprise dominance, raising the stakes for every smaller AI company's partnership and differentiation strategy.

The model features native multimodality for text, image, video, and desktop computer operation, and is currently available via API with announced token subscription plans.

The model supports a context window of up to 1,000,000 tokens using the MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) architecture.

Token subscription plans include Plus ($20/mo for ~1.7B tokens), Max ($50/mo for ~5.1B tokens), and Ultra ($120/mo for ~9.8B tokens).
The model was trained on a data pipeline scaled to over 100T tokens with native multimodal alignment from step zero.

synthesis.emailSubject: DeepMind's Gemma 4 12B brings native audio to laptops

content.what_changed: Google DeepMind released Gemma 4 12B, a 12-billion-parameter unified, encoder-free multimodal model that natively accepts text, images, audio, and video inputs. The model and its instruction-tuned variant are released under an Apache 2.0 license and are designed to run locally on consumer hardware with 16 GB of VRAM or unified memory.
key_facts: The model features 12 billion parameters (Gemma 4 12B).
The official release date was June 3, 2026.
The model is released under the Apache 2.0 license.
Weights are distributed via Hugging Face and Kaggle, with the instruction-tuned variant named google/gemma-4-12B-it.
Hardware requirements specify that the model can run on consumer laptops with 16 GB of VRAM or unified memory.
content.bd_relevance: Gemma 4 12B materially lowers barriers to integrating high-quality multimodal models into on-device products and partner stacks, while its Apache 2.0 licensing makes commercial integration straightforward for local-agent and edge SDK vendors.
content.headline: Google DeepMind releases Gemma 4 12B — a 12B encoder-free multimodal model with native audio that runs on 16GB laptops (Apache 2.0).
content.why_it_matters: This release signals a push toward democratizing advanced multimodal intelligence at the edge, accelerating competition in on-device and low-latency AI. Companies providing device SDKs or offline agent platforms are advantaged, while closed-weight cloud incumbents face increased pressure from open, locally deployable alternatives.
